what_was_done: Item 52 of topics/platform-proven-3.md no longer cites the empty permission_denials: its evidence is the PostToolUse lines of leg A (Read outside the working directory, Write, Read and Edit in the linked worktree, the compound git add and commit) and git (e2b67c6 on story/x; a61f0a6 in the check's rerun). It records the fact in bold: a refused call of a workflow step does not appear in the session result's permission_denials (leg D R3CTRL on 2.1.332, default mode, tool list 'Workflow Bash(echo *)', D-result.json permission_denials [] with subtype success; the round-4 rerun A the same on 2.1.331); it shows in the step transcript as a tool_result with is_error true and 'This command requires approval', and as a PreToolUse payload with no PostToolUse. Item 50 keeps the citation where it is evidence (a main-session call, item 30) and says it is none for a step. Added from the same step transcripts, read when the record was corrected and marked as not cited by CHECK.md: the transcript record's permissionDecision key (reject from source config for the refused call, reject from source hook for a hook's block, accept for an admitted call, absent for a call cut off by a budget stop), in a five-row table, so that a driver can tell a refusal from the other traces. platform.md gains the headless duty 'A step's refusal (item 52) is not in permission_denials: the driver reads the step transcripts'.

The sentence 'The first run's tool list covers the story step's write scope' is gone. Item 52 lists what one step did and says 'no more than this was shown': one Read of a plugin file outside the working directory, one Write (type create), one Read and one Edit in a linked worktree under the project, and one compound Bash call (git add and git commit) there, each with its PostToolUse line; the rerun the same calls. It names what was not shown: Glob, Grep or Agent under a bare name, a write outside the project, a second step. The item's heading and the index row of platform.md say 'bare tool names' and no longer 'cross-boundary work'.

Item 53 now says a main-session tool payload carries the session's effort: the PreToolUse and PostToolUse of the Workflow call carry medium in leg A and in the check's rerun, and low in leg D, whose session ran at low. The false sentence 'The main session's own Workflow events carry no effort key' is gone. PR5-1 in sources/extra-probes-5.json says the same ('a main-session payload carries the session's effort (medium)'). The same fact stated elsewhere was corrected: item 48 of topics/platform-proven-2.md now ends 'a step's payload carries the effort the step was dispatched with, a main-session payload the session's'.

Item 53 is retitled 'a step's payloads carry the effort the step was dispatched with' and gives both runs: the prober's (session medium, agent file low, agent() call low: 16 payloads low, which cannot say whose value it is) and the check's rerun (agent file xhigh, call low, session medium: all 14 step payloads low), so the payload carries the dispatched effort, not the session's and not the agent file's. The claim that this settles item 26 is withdrawn: no step was dispatched without an effort, so whether such a step takes its agent file's effort is not shown, and the design does not rely on it (conventions.md: every step sets model and effort). platform.md row 26 therefore reads 'Open | Unprobed, not relied on: every step is dispatched with its effort, which its payloads carry (item 53)' in place of 'Proven | ... the agent file's effort'. Item 48 of platform-proven-2.md no longer says round 5 'settled it'.

Item 54 is rewritten as 'two shapes, and the cap is soft'. Shape 1 (cap 0.05, the prober's run and the check's rerun B): the spend crossed the cap only with the main loop's second answer, after the workflow had ended; run record completed with the whole return value, every agent done, standard error empty. Shape 2 (cap 0.02, the check's rerun only, said so): standard error 'Budget limit reached ($0.05 of $0.02); stopping background agents.', run record killed, result null, error 'Workflow aborted', the first step left in state progress with lastToolName StructuredOutput, later steps never started, journal with no result line, and the step's StructuredOutput PreToolUse in the hook log with no PostToolUse. The cap is soft: $0.0578 and $0.0651 on a 5-cent cap, $0.0544 on a 2-cent cap (2.7 times); a large step's overshoot is stated as not measured. PR5-1 describes both shapes the same way. platform.md's headless bullet no longer says 'A budget stop is not a dead run': it says the driver reads the run record, 'completed with the whole result or killed with its step lost', and that the cap is soft.

'Empty result text' is gone from item 54 and from PR5-1. Both now say the session result of a budget stop has no result key at all, with errors ['Reached maximum budget ($<cap>)'] and terminal_reason budget_exhausted, in both shapes; item 54 adds that a driver therefore reads result.get("result"). platform.md's headless bullet says 'has no result key'.

Item 55 no longer gives a naming rule. It says the folder is found by the session id: every hook payload's transcript_path is the folder's path plus .jsonl, or a reader globs projects/*/<session id>/, so no rule is relied on; and that of the name only this was shown: each '/' and each '.' of the absolute project path becomes '-', no probed path holding any other character outside letters, digits and '-'. It adds the journal's real shape (one launched line for the run, then a started and a result line per agent; 'failed' for a failed step, seen in leg D's journal; none for a step cut off), the repeated tool_use entries (assistant records hold them all; api-request-blob records repeat some: leg A 8 ids in 10 entries; a reader takes the assistant records or dedupes by id), that workflowProgress starts with workflow_phase entries, and that a killed record has result null and adds a key error. The header says which folders were compared (the kept round-4 folder, leg A's, the three reruns') and that legs B and D's records and journals agree.

Item 37 of topics/platform-proven-2.md now gives the closed-schema failure per version: 2.1.331 (rerun A) four refusals, then after about 190 s 'subagent completed without calling StructuredOutput (after in-conversation nudge)'; 2.1.332 (round 5, leg D, run once and not rerun) five attempts in about 10 s, each seen by the hook, then 'StructuredOutput retry cap (5) exceeded — 5 failed calls with no valid output — last StructuredOutput error:' and the schema message, the step's state error and the workflow completed. It adds that the open and declared legs held unchanged on 2.1.332. The header of platform-proven-3.md no longer says the closed-schema failure 're-held': its leg D section lists what held again (items 36, 37's open and declared legs, 38's Bash leg and control, 40, 48) and what changed (37's closed-schema leg: another count, error and time).

platform-proven-3.md has a section 'Leg D — the round-4 rerun A, run again on 2.1.332', placed where the rerun is cited. It records the three deviations: entered by the typed workflow command where the round-4 rerun went through the skill probecall; run under the two isolation flags, the sandbox-off --settings flag and the ceiling variable, none of which the round-4 rerun carried (tool list 'Workflow Bash(echo *)', session effort low); and R3B's rewrite not rebuilt, so that on this version item 38's StructuredOutput leg rests on R2A and R2B. It also says the round-5 check read leg D's logs and did not rerun it.

The caps: first-run.md 3.5's --max-budget-usd row is 'Item 54: a soft cap; two shapes of stop (3.7)', D14 says both caps are soft, and ORDER.md has a sentence under the caps table (in flight is charged past a cap, 2.7 times a 2-cent cap in the probe, so one attempt's overshoot can take a session past its cap and the run past its total). Two corrections beyond the proposed text, both needed for the diagnosis to be right. (1) budget_stop moves up the 'first that applies' list, after blocked_before_first_turn, in first-run.md 3.7 and in ORDER.md's table: a stop that kills the survey step would otherwise be named tier_not_applied or no_workflow. (2) 'Resume with --dir' alone would always be refused: a stop comes only after the cap is passed, so the recorded cost plus the same cap is over refusal 8's default total. D14, ORDER.md's row and the test say a resume at the same cap needs --total. Test: test_budget_stop_shapes (both shapes, no result key: exit 1, budget_stop, the record printed, --total in the resume line); section 6 lists PR5-1 and PR5C-16.
